title_en: Beijing Zhiyang Weibo Technology Development Co., Ltd. v. Chuangsi Biotechnology Engineering (Dongguan) Co., Ltd. and Kaifeng City Administration Bureau of Henan Province — dispute over intermediation contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. full_text_en:
Beijing Zhiyang Weibo Technology Development Co., Ltd. v. Chuangsi Biotechnology Engineering (Dongguan) Co., Ltd. and Kaifeng City Administration Bureau, Henan Province — dispute over intermediary contract

【Ruling Summary】

1. When a plaintiff in a civil action names multiple defendants at the time of filing the complaint, and the domicile of one of those defendants falls within the jurisdiction of the people's court accepting the case, that court may determine jurisdiction based on the defendant's domicile. If another defendant believes that the accepting people's court lacks jurisdiction, it should raise an objection to jurisdiction during the first-instance defense period. If no such objection is raised during this period, because the case has entered substantive trial and jurisdiction has been established, even if the defendant located within the jurisdiction of the accepting people's court is not the proper defendant in the case, the people's court may rule to dismiss the plaintiff's claim against that defendant. This does not affect the substantive trial of the case, and there is no need to transfer jurisdiction.

2. The place of performance of a contract refers to the place where the primary obligations of the contract are performed. The place of performance of the primary obligations of an intermediary contract should be determined as the place where the intermediary conduct occurred.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2008) Min Shen Zi No. 1364

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chuangsi Biotechnology Engineering (Dongguan) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Gaobao Green Technology City, Santang Management Zone, Changping Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Huang Jianjun, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Song Min, lawyer at Beijing Zhongji Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Zhiyang Weibo Technology Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 26, Sixth Street, Yongle Economic Development Zone, Tongzhou District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Guo Yiqun, Chairman of the Board.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Kaifeng City Administration Bureau, domiciled at No. 2, Yingbin Road, Kaifeng City, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Chen Chuanzhi, Director.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Kejun, lawyer at Henan Zhengyan Law Firm.

Regarding the dispute over an intermediary contract between Chuangsi Biotechnology Engineering (Dongguan) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chuangsi Company) and Beijing Zhiyang Weibo Technology Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhiyang Company) and Kaifeng City Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Kaifeng Administration Bureau), the High People's Court of Henan Province rendered (2007) Yu Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 166 civil judgment on June 12, 2008, which has become legally effective. On December 4, 2008, Chuangsi Company applied to this Court for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review the case, and the review is now concluded.

Chuangsi Company claims in its application for retrial: 1. The first-instance and second-instance judgments suffer from the issue that the defendant Kaifeng Administration Bureau is not a proper party. The cause of action in this case is a contract dispute, and the factual basis for the court's judgment is also the "Agreement" signed on February 27, 2006 between the applicant for retrial Chuangsi Company and the respondent Zhiyang Company. The signatories to that "Agreement" are only two parties, namely the applicant for retrial and the respondent. Although the words "Investor (Kaifeng City Administration Bureau)" appear in that "Agreement," the respondent Kaifeng Administration Bureau is not a signatory to the "Agreement," so there is no civil legal relationship between the respondent Kaifeng Administration Bureau and the respondent Zhiyang Company, and the respondent Kaifeng Administration Bureau is unrelated to the contract dispute in this case. In order to obtain jurisdiction before the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province, the respondent (plaintiff at first instance) Zhiyang Company erroneously listed the respondent Kaifeng Administration Bureau as a defendant at first instance in this contract dispute. The first-instance and second-instance courts, without any factual or legal basis, still listed Kaifeng Administration Bureau as a defendant. Although Kaifeng Administration Bureau repeatedly emphasized in its defense that it was unrelated to the case, the first-instance and second-instance courts ignored this and still listed it as a defendant. Therefore, there is only one defendant in this case, namely the applicant for retrial Chuangsi Company, and the first-instance and second-instance judgments suffer from the issue that the defendant Kaifeng Administration Bureau is not a proper party. 2. This case violates legal provisions and has a jurisdictional error. The cause of action in this case is a contract dispute, with only one defendant, the applicant for retrial Chuangsi Company. According to Article 24 of the Civil Procedure Law, an action arising from a contract dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the defendant's domicile or the place of performance of the contract. Therefore, the court with jurisdiction over this case should be the people's court of the defendant's domicile — the people's court of the domicile of the applicant for retrial (defendant at first instance) Chuangsi Company — and the people's court of the place of performance of the contract — the people's court of the domicile of the respondent Zhiyang Company. None of the above-mentioned courts with jurisdiction is the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province or the High People's Court of Henan Province. 3. The judgment lacks factual basis. The first-instance and second-instance courts improperly handled the claim of Zhiyang Company against Kaifeng Administration Bureau. The second-instance judgment lacks factual basis. 4. The second-instance judgment incorrectly applied the law.

The respondent Zhiyang Company and the respondent Kaifeng Administration Bureau did not submit written opinions.

This Court holds: According to Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law, when a people's court accepts a civil action, the requirement for the defendant is that there is "a specific defendant." When the plaintiff at first instance, Zhiyang Company, filed the complaint, it listed both Chuangsi Company and Kaifeng Administration Bureau as defendants, which satisfies the requirement of specificity of the defendant under the Civil Procedure Law. Because the domicile of Kaifeng Administration Bureau is within the jurisdiction of the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court, it was not improper for the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court to determine jurisdiction based on the defendant's domicile when accepting the case. If Chuangsi Company believed that the Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court lacked jurisdiction over this case, it had the right to raise an objection to jurisdiction during the first-instance defense period, and if dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, it could also appeal through the second-instance procedure to assert its claim. However, upon review of the first-instance case file, this Court finds that the applicant for retrial, Chuangsi Company, did not raise an objection to jurisdiction during the first-instance defense period. After the case entered substantive trial, because jurisdiction had already been established, whether Kaifeng Administration Bureau is a proper defendant does not affect the first-instance court's trial of the case. Even if the people's court finds that Kaifeng Administration Bureau is not a proper defendant in this case and rules to dismiss Zhiyang Company's claim against Kaifeng Administration Bureau, this does not affect the substantive trial proceedings that have already begun, and there is no need to transfer the case. Furthermore, the place of performance of a contract refers to the place where the primary obligations of the contract are performed. In this case, the place of performance of the primary obligations of the intermediary contract should be the place where the intermediary conduct occurred. Based on the contents of the thank-you letter from Lai Zhiwen, a project participant of Chuangsi Company, to Guo Yiqun, Chairman of Zhiyang Company, as found by the original trial, regarding Zhiyang Company's reception of senior management of Chuangsi Company in Kaifeng City and its assistance to Chuangsi Company in bidding for the Kaifeng project, Kaifeng City, as the location of the project that is the subject of the intermediary contract, can be determined as the place of performance of the intermediary contract in this case. The Kaifeng Intermediate People's Court may accordingly exercise jurisdiction. According to Article 14 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, violations of exclusive jurisdiction, specialized jurisdiction, and other serious illegal exercises of jurisdiction shall be deemed by the people's court as "jurisdictional error" under Article 179, paragraph 1, item (7) of the Civil Procedure Law. In this case, the first-instance court is the court of the domicile of the defendant listed in the complaint, and also the court of the place of performance of the contract, which does not constitute a serious illegal exercise of jurisdiction. Therefore, the applicant for retrial's claim that the original judgment violated legal provisions and had a jurisdictional error cannot be established, and this Court does not support it. Regarding the issue of whether the respondent Kaifeng Administration Bureau is a proper defendant, as stated above, after jurisdiction is established, whether Kaifeng Administration Bureau is a proper defendant does not affect the substantive trial of this case. Moreover, neither the first-instance nor the second-instance judgment imposed substantive obligations on Kaifeng Administration Bureau, and this did not affect the correct judgment of the case. This does not meet the conditions for initiating a retrial under the "circumstances where a violation of legal procedures may affect the correct judgment or ruling of the case" as provided in Article 179, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law. As for the applicant for retrial's claims that the judgment lacks factual basis and incorrectly applies the law, because the applicant for retrial only listed these two statutory grounds without explaining the facts and reasons on which they are based and did not provide sufficient evidence to support them, this Court does not recognize them. In summary, according to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial of Chuangsi Biotechnology Engineering (Dongguan) Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Gao Ke
Acting Judge: Wang Shengquan
Acting Judge: Liu Xiaofei

April 1, 2009

Clerk: Shao Haiqiang

【Introduction to the Presiding Judge】
Gao Ke, Senior Judge: Born in 1968, Master of Laws, served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court from 2006.
